STATUS: WORK MERGED. CLOSE BLOCKED ONLY ON UNTICKED AC CHECKBOXES — a 10-minute job, not more work.

Change 1255 is MERGED (bb67d4f7f2 on gerrit/main), LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1. Four evidence
comments are on this ticket, including the full mutation ledger.

TWO CLOSE ATTEMPTS, both mechanical rather than substantive:
 1. First failed for a missing `--class` (this is a bug ticket). `--class preexisting` is the right
    value: the COVERAGE GAP this ticket names predated the work, and the work filled it.
 2. Second failed because the description's `- [ ]` items are still unticked. rebar requires the author
    to confirm each one and tick the box, so closing means editing the description.

I DELIBERATELY DID NOT TICK THEM. The implementing agent's evidence appears to cover every item —
including the one the gate quoted back ("the structural anti-regression guard is extended to cover
`adapters/jira/acli_graph.py`"), which its mutation ledger demonstrates: adding a fourth unpaginated
reader (`get_status_map`) FAILS the guard, naming the file and line. But I have not verified all six
items individually, and ticking a box is an assertion that the item is done. Whoever closes this should
read the four evidence comments, tick what they can confirm, and either finish or `[operator-attested]`
anything that is genuinely out-of-snapshot.

THE HEADLINE RESULT, so nobody re-litigates the premise: **Cloud pages CORRECTLY.** Its whole-project
readers (`acli_graph.py` get_parent_map :215, get_comment_map :318, get_issuelinks_map :412) use an
OPAQUE CURSOR (`nextPageToken` + `isLast`), not offset arithmetic, so the DC bug family
(advance-by-requested-size, break-on-short-page) structurally cannot occur here. Measured before any
test was written: 250 items at 100/page -> 250 recovered; pages capped at 40 while 100 requested ->
still 250 recovered in 7 requests. So this ticket's deliverable is a REGRESSION NET, not a bug fix —
and the net has teeth: transplanting the DC bug into Cloud's loop is caught by a dedicated short-page
oracle that no other assertion in the suite catches.

IT DID FIND A REAL DEFECT, filed separately as [rebar:cabc-7a98-d173-4d7c]: a server that repeats its
cursor token makes these three readers SPIN FOREVER (byte-identical request -> identical response ->
neither break fires), and the fail-open `except Exception` then converts it into a silently partial
map. `fetcher._iter_pages` already has exactly this guard at `fetcher.py:286-308`
(`SilentTruncationError(reason="same-token-twice")`); these readers do not. AC4's oracle is committed as
`xfail(strict=True)` citing that bug, so it flips RED the moment the guard lands. Cloud-side; does NOT
gate e369.
